fields.Participants: Requesting Department Head, VP Store Operations, COO, CIO
fields.Trigger: Identified need for capital investment (new store, renovation, equipment, IT project)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-submit of "submits capex request in ERP" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "Supporting documentation attached" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "System validates completeness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-361 (ensure controlled execution — Capital Expenditure Request & Approval (PA-40.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Weak-justification risk**: requests approved on narrative enthusiasm without quantified benefit; mitigated by mandatory business-case fields and documentation (steps 1–2)
- **Cost-underestimate risk**: estimates anchored optimistically to ease approval; mitigated by reasonableness validation and the W1812 financial evaluation (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Capex request form in ERP — project description, justification, cost estimate, category (step 1)
- Supporting documentation attachment — site plans, lease summaries, financial models per W1652 (step 2)
- System completeness validation before routing (step 3)
Time Estimate: 2–4 days elapsed per occurrence (1–2 days + 1–2 days) — at ~30–50 capex requests/year ≈ 30–50 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Requesting Department Head submits capex request in ERP: (a) project name and description, (b) business justification: why needed, what problem solved, what opportunity captured, (c) capex type: new store construction, store renovation, DC expansion, IT infrastructure, vehicle/fleet, equipment replacement, (d) estimated total cost (breakdown: materials, labor, equipment, services, contingency 10–15%), (e) expected timeline: start date, milestones, completion date, (f) expected benefits: revenue increase, cost reduction, risk mitigation, compliance requirement, (g) priority: mandatory (regulatory/safety), growth (new revenue), maintenance (renewal/replacement), discretionary

Supporting documentation attached: (a) for new stores: site plan, lease summary, financial model per W1652, (b) for IT projects: vendor proposals, technical specifications, implementation plan, (c) for renovations: scope of work, contractor quotes, before/after photos, (d) for equipment: vendor quotes (minimum 2 for items > PHP 500K), technical specifications, installation requirements

System validates completeness: (a) all required fields populated, (b) supporting documents attached, (c) cost estimate within reasonable range (system flags outliers vs. historical benchmarks), (d) request routed to financial evaluation per W1812

workflows.name: Capex Financial Evaluation & Business Case Review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "discount at company's weighted average cost of capital" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews against annual capex budget affordability" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prepares financial evaluation summary" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: FP&A review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Assumption-optimism risk**: rosier assumptions than the W1645 corporate baseline inflate returns; mitigated by assumption disclosure in the summary (step 3)
- **Alternative-blindness risk**: a project approved when a cheaper alternative (lease vs. build) serves better; mitigated by explicit alternatives evaluation (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - Financial evaluation model — total investment cost, NPV, IRR, payback per project (step 1)
- Strategic alignment assessment vs. Board priorities and alternatives (step 2)
- Evaluation summary with recommendation and key assumptions (step 3)
Time Estimate: 1 day elapsed per occurrence (1 day) — at ~30–50 evaluations/year ≈ 30–50 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: FP&A performs financial evaluation: (a) **total investment cost**: all capitalized costs including materials, labor, equipment, installation, testing, project management, (b) **operating cash flows**: incremental revenue, cost savings, or avoided costs per year for project life, (c) **net present value (NPV)**: discount at company's weighted average cost of capital (WACC ~10–12% for Philippine retail), (d) **internal rate of return (IRR)**: target > 15% for growth projects; no minimum for mandatory/regulatory, (e) **payback period**: target < 3 years for stores; < 2 years for IT/equipment, (f) **sensitivity analysis**: NPV at -10% revenue, +10% cost, 1-year delay

FP&A assesses strategic alignment: (a) maps to Board-approved strategic priorities per W1645, (b) evaluates against alternative uses of capital (opportunity cost), (c) considers timing: can this be deferred without significant impact? (d) reviews against annual capex budget affordability (total requested vs. available capital)

FP&A prepares financial evaluation summary: (a) recommendation: approve, approve with conditions, defer, reject, (b) key assumptions and risks, (c) comparison to similar completed projects (actual vs. projected returns)

fields.Participants: Department Head, FP&A, CFO, CEO, Board

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Approval workflow in system" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "center and entity assignment" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - operational: Approver per DOA matrix review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Approval-bypass risk**: spending begins before authorization; mitigated by system gating — no project number, no PO (steps 2, 4)
- **Ambiguous-conditions risk**: verbal conditions never enforced; mitigated by documented conditions tracked to satisfaction before commitment (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Tiered approval routing per DOA (W1732) — CFO < PHP 1M; CEO PHP 1–10M; Board committee/Board above (step 1)
- Sequential system workflow — FP&A → CFO → CEO → Board with audit trail (step 2)
- Conditions-of-approval capture (scope reduction, quotes, revised timeline) (step 3)
- Capex project creation — CPX-YYYY-NNN number, budget, timeline (step 4)
Time Estimate: 3–13 days elapsed per occurrence (1–5 days + 1–5 days + 1–3 days) — at ~30–50 approvals/year ≈ 30–50 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Tiered approval per Delegation of Authority per W1732: (a) < PHP 1M: CFO approval (based on FP&A recommendation), (b) PHP 1M–10M: CEO approval (CFO endorses), (c) PHP 10M–50M: Board committee approval (Executive Committee), (d) > PHP 50M: Full Board approval (presented at board meeting per W1714)

Approval workflow in system: (a) request routed sequentially: FP&A → CFO → CEO → Board committee → Board (depending on amount), (b) each approver reviews financial evaluation and supporting documents in system, (c) approver records decision: approved, approved with conditions, deferred, rejected — with comments, (d) system enforces approval limits (approver cannot exceed DOA threshold)

Conditions of approval (if any): (a) reduce scope to fit budget, (b) obtain additional vendor quotes, (c) revise timeline, (d) phase the project over 2+ years, (e) funding source reallocation (defer another project)

Approved request creates capex project in system: (a) unique project number (format: CPX-YYYY-NNN), (b) approved budget, (c) project timeline and milestones, (d) cost center and entity assignment, (e) budget reserved against annual capex plan per W1648

fields.Volume: ~30–50 active capex projects at any time

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-assign of "allocates approved budget to capex project" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews all active capex projects" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: FP&A review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Commitment-blindness risk**: overruns hidden in issued-but-uninvoiced POs; mitigated by committed + incurred tracking (step 2)
- **Portfolio-skew risk**: early projects consume the annual envelope, starving later priorities; mitigated by quarterly portfolio review (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Budget allocation by cost category — construction, equipment, materials, professional fees, contingency (step 1)
- Committed vs. incurred cost tracking — POs issued vs. invoiced (step 2)
- Monthly portfolio review — utilization % vs. completion %, variance (step 3)
- Quarterly Board capex portfolio report (step 4)
Time Estimate: 1 day elapsed per occurrence (1 day); cadence-carried steps as authored (Continuous, 1–2 days/month, Quarterly) — cadence: Continuous; annual effort is event-driven (annualize at realized volume).

steps.activity: FP&A allocates approved budget to capex project: (a) breaks down total budget by cost category: construction, equipment, materials, services, contingency, (b) assigns entity: which of the 5 legal entities bears the cost, (c) links to funding source: retained earnings, bank loan, lease financing

System tracks committed costs: (a) **committed**: POs issued for the project (not yet received/invoiced), (b) **incurred**: invoices received and matched to PO/GR, (c) **paid**: payments made to vendors/contractors, (d) **remaining budget**: approved budget − committed − incurred, (e) **forecast to complete**: Project Manager estimate of remaining costs

Monthly: FP&A reviews all active capex projects: (a) budget utilization (% spent vs. % complete), (b) cost variance (actual vs. budget at current completion), (c) schedule variance (actual vs. planned milestones), (d) forecast to complete vs. remaining budget, (e) flag: projects trending > 110% of budget

Quarterly: CFO presents capex portfolio status to Board: (a) total capex spent vs. annual budget, (b) major project updates (new stores, DC, IT), (c) budget overruns and corrective actions, (d) revised full-year capex forecast

fields.Trigger: Project scope change, cost increase, or timeline extension

workflows.name: Capex Request Revision & Scope Change Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-request of "requested by Store Operations" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-submit of "submits change order request" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "FP&A evaluates change order" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: Project Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: change orders approved piecemeal until economics invert; mitigated by revised NPV/IRR evaluation per change (step 3)
- **Contingency-exhaustion risk**: contingency silently consumed by routine changes; mitigated by contingency visibility in every evaluation (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Change order request workflow — description, reason, cost impact (step 2)
- FP&A evaluation — revised returns, contingency availability (step 3)
- Revised budget tracking post-approval (step 4)
Time Estimate: 2–4 days elapsed per occurrence (1–2 days + 1–2 days); cadence-carried steps as authored (Event-driven) — at ~10–20 revisions/year ≈ 10–20 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Project Manager identifies need for scope change: (a) construction discovers unforeseen site conditions (common in Philippine construction — soil issues, utility relocation), (b) vendor price increase since original quote, (c) design change requested by Store Operations, (d) regulatory requirement not initially anticipated, (e) scope reduction opportunity (value engineering)

Project Manager submits change order request: (a) description of change, (b) reason for change, (c) cost impact (increase or decrease), (d) schedule impact, (e) revised total project cost and timeline

FP&A evaluates change order: (a) revised NPV/IRR if revenue impact, (b) revised budget vs. available contingency, (c) if within original budget + contingency (< 10% increase): CFO approves, (d) if exceeding contingency or > 10% budget increase: requires approval per W1813 tiers
System updates project budget with approved change order; revised budget tracked going forward

fields.Trigger: Urgent capital need (equipment failure, safety issue, storm damage, regulatory order)

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow notification of "contacts CEO/CFO directly" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documentation completed within 5 business days" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-capture of "entered in system" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-361 (ensure controlled execution — Capital Expenditure Request & Approval (PA-40.1).)
- operational: Department Head review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Emergency-label-abuse risk**: non-urgent requests routed as emergencies to skip evaluation; mitigated by retroactive review and Board visibility (step 4)
- **Paper-trail-gap risk**: verbal approvals never documented; mitigated by mandatory retroactive system entry (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Emergency triggers and direct CEO/CFO contact path (steps 1–2)
- Verbal approval with emergency procurement authorization (step 3)
- Retroactive formalization with "Emergency" designation and Board notification (step 4)
Time Estimate: ~3–6 hours per emergency capex event (direct CEO/CFO contact 1–2 hours + same-day verbal approval and procurement authorization + retroactive formal approval within 5 days) × ~5–10 events/year ≈ 15–60 hours/year.

steps.activity: Emergency triggers: (a) store HVAC failure in summer (cannot operate without cooling in Philippine heat), (b) typhoon damage to store structure, (c) forklift failure at DC (halts operations), (d) BIR order to upgrade POS system (compliance deadline), (e) fire damage to store or DC
Department Head contacts CEO/CFO directly (phone/email): (a) describes emergency, (b) estimated cost, (c) business impact of delay, (d) proposed solution and timeline

CEO provides verbal approval; CFO authorizes emergency procurement: (a) procurement can proceed without full financial evaluation (W1812 bypassed), (b) PO issued with emergency flag, (c) retroactive documentation completed within 5 business days (full capex request, financial evaluation, formal approval)
Retroactive formal approval completed; project entered in system with "Emergency" designation; Board informed at next meeting if amount > PHP 10M

fields.Trigger: Capex request approved (W1813); procurement ready to proceed

workflows.name: Capex Requisition to Purchase Order Conversion

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "Procurement converts approved capex request to purchase requisition" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-issue of "issued with delivery terms aligned to project timeline" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approver verifies that capex project exists and has budget" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-361 (ensure controlled execution — Capital Expenditure Request & Approval (PA-40.1).)
- operational: Procurement review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unlinked-PO risk**: project POs booked outside the capex project, understating spend; mitigated by PO referencing the CPX project number with auto-commit (step 3)
- **Bid-threshold-splitting risk**: packages carved below the PHP 500K bid threshold; mitigated by package-level review in sourcing (steps 1–2)
System Touchpoints: - Requisition conversion with procurement packaging (construction, equipment, services) (step 1)
- Vendor sourcing — competitive bid > PHP 500K, minimum 3 quotes (step 2)
- PO-to-project linkage with automatic budget commitment (step 3)
Time Estimate: Per capex project ~3–5 days of procurement effort (request-to-requisition conversion 1–3 days + vendor sourcing over 1–4 weeks elapsed; PO-to-project budget commitment automated) × ~30–50 projects/year ≈ 90–250 days/year at ~100–200 capex POs.

steps.activity: Procurement converts approved capex request to purchase requisition: (a) breaks project into procurement packages (construction, equipment, services), (b) each package becomes a separate PO with vendor, items, quantities, prices, (c) PO references capex project number for cost tracking

Procurement sources vendors per standard procurement process: (a) competitive bid for items > PHP 500K (minimum 3 quotes), (b) negotiated contract for construction (per VS-03), (c) select best value (not just lowest cost — consider quality, timeline, warranty), (d) PO issued with delivery terms aligned to project timeline

PO linked to capex project: (a) system auto-commits PO amount against project budget, (b) project budget report shows: committed (POs), incurred (invoices), remaining, (c) PO approval per standard DOA (not capex DOA — PO approver verifies that capex project exists and has budget)

fields.Trigger: Capex request created; maintained throughout project lifecycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of the "Required documentation per capex project" checklist (replaces manual Step 1 assembly).
- System auto-refresh of the CIP project record from posted transactions (maintains the automated Step 2 feed).
- System auto-review of "reviews capex documentation during annual audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-361 (ensure controlled execution — Capital Expenditure Request & Approval (PA-40.1).)
- operational: FP&A review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Audit-trail-break risk**: approvals happen outside the system (email/verbal) leaving gaps; mitigated by system-workflow routing as the approval channel (step 2)
- **Document-scatter risk**: approvals and evaluations filed in personal drives; mitigated by the project documentation set retention (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Project documentation set — request, business case, evaluation, approvals, change orders (step 1)
- System audit trail — submitter/reviewer/approver with timestamps (step 2)
- External auditor sample review against DOA (step 3)
Time Estimate: Capex documentation assembly continuous within project administration across ~30–50 projects/year (approval audit trail automated); external-audit sample support ≈ 2–3 days/year at the annual audit.

steps.activity: Required documentation per capex project: (a) original request with business case and financial evaluation, (b) approval documentation (system approval trail or board resolution), (c) vendor quotes and selection rationale, (d) POs linked to project, (e) change orders with approval, (f) progress reports and milestone confirmations, (g) completion certificate and asset turnover documentation per W1827, (h) post-implementation review per W2748

System maintains complete audit trail: (a) who submitted, reviewed, approved at each stage, (b) dates and timestamps, (c) version history for revised requests, (d) linked documents accessible from project record

External auditor reviews capex documentation during annual audit: (a) sample of capex projects: verify approval per DOA, verify cost capitalization per PFRS, verify project completion and asset turnover, (b) assess internal controls over capex process
